theme: The LORD reigns; let the earth rejoice
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 97. It is another enthronement psalm. Notice how creation and the nations respond to the arrival of the King, and how the psalm ends with joy for the righteous.
settingTheScene: Psalm 97 continues the theme of the previous psalm: the LORD reigns. It uses imagery of theophany (God’s appearing), with clouds, fire, lightning, and melting mountains, similar to Sinai. It also speaks of the humiliation of idols and the joy of God’s people. It reads like a commentary on Revelation 19, where the multitude cries, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns,” and the idols and the powers of evil are overthrown.
observation: “The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the many coastlands be glad!” (v. 1).
“Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne” (v. 2).
“The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth” (v. 5).
“The heavens proclaim his righteousness, and all the peoples see his glory” (v. 6).
“All worshipers of images are put to shame” (v. 7).
“O you who love the LORD, hate evil! He preserves the lives of his saints” (v. 10).
“Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart” (v. 11).
“Rejoice in the LORD, O you righteous, and give thanks to his holy name!” (v. 12).
interpretation:
Where Psalm 93 spoke of the stability of God’s reign, Psalm 97 shows its effects. The first response is joy: “The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the many coastlands be glad!” Even distant lands are invited. But the reign of God is also awesome: “Clouds and thick darkness are all around him; righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.” God’s throne rests on righteousness and justice; he rules fairly. “Fire goes before him and burns up his adversaries all around. His lightnings light up the world; the earth sees and trembles. The mountains melt like wax before the LORD.” This is similar to the plagues and cosmic disturbances of Revelation. The Lord’s coming is overwhelming, and all of creation responds.

“The heavens proclaim his righteousness, and all the peoples see his glory.” Then a result for false religion: “All worshipers of images are put to shame, who make their boast in worthless idols; worship him, all you gods!” Idols are shown to be empty. The gods themselves are told to worship the LORD, a statement that echoes Revelation, where the demonic powers are defeated. Zion hears and is glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoice “because of your judgments, O LORD.” God’s judgments are a cause of rejoicing for his people, because they mean justice at last. “For you, O LORD, are most high over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.”

Then the moral application: “O you who love the LORD, hate evil! He preserves the lives of his saints; he delivers them from the hand of the wicked.” Love for God and hatred of evil go together. And the promise: “Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.” The metaphor is of seeds in the ground: light and joy are planted for the righteous and will spring up. It may not look like it now, in a world that persecutes the saints, but a harvest of light and joy is coming. This is the same theme as in Revelation 21, where there is no more night and no more tears.

The final invitation is to rejoice: “Rejoice in the LORD, O you righteous, and give thanks to his holy name!” Believers face the future with joy. In Revelation, the final celebration is of the marriage supper of the Lamb. For now, we rejoice by faith, trusting that the day will come when the evidence matches the promise.
connection: Exodus 19:16-19 and Psalm 18:7-15 describe God’s appearing. Psalm 96, 98, and 99 are other enthronement psalms. Isaiah 42:17 and 44:9-20 mock idols. Hebrews 1:6 quotes the Septuagint of verse 7, “Let all God’s angels worship him.” Psalm 89:14 says righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne. Revelation 19:1-8 shows the multitude rejoicing at God’s judgments. Romans 12:9 says to abhor what is evil. Psalm 126:5-6 speaks of sowing with tears and reaping with joy. Revelation 21:23-25 pictures the city without need of the sun. Habakkuk 3:3-6 is another theophany.
application:
Think of a situation where you cannot yet see justice, and picture “light sown” there. Pray for the harvest.

Hate what God hates this week. Ask him to show you something you have been tolerating.

Rejoice in the LORD today, even if circumstances are hard, and give thanks to his holy name.
prayerPrompts: Thank him for light sown for the righteous.
Ask him to give you gladness in him.
